_comment: Baseline numbers for benchmark regression detection.
Captured: macOS, Apple Silicon (M-series), Go 1.26, 18 cores.
Each value is the median of 3 runs at -benchtime=3s.
Tolerance contract: per-package TestBenchmarkRegression fails when
the AVERAGE ratio across that package's checked benchmarks exceeds
1 + tolerance_avg_pct/100. Per-bench drift is logged but doesn't
fail the test alone (jitter washes out over an average).
Tolerance is tight (3%) but the gate only runs when TALON_BENCH=1
is set in the environment AND packages are serialized via -p=1.
`make test` does both. Plain `go test ./...` skips the gate
because parallel package execution under default GOMAXPROCS
produces 50%+ contention spikes that swamp any reasonable
regression threshold — false-positive city.
Runtime escape hatches:
- go test -short    : skips regression tests entirely
- TALON_BENCH_SKIP=1: ditto (for CI on heterogeneous hardware)
Outlier safeguard: any single bench at 2× baseline DOES fail the
test individually — that signals a real bug, not jitter.
Regenerate after deliberate changes:
go test -bench=. -benchmem -run=^$ -benchtime=3s -count=3 \
./internal/config/ ./internal/server/ ./internal/agentcontext/
Take the median ns/op per bench, update the rows here.
